newsitem.title: POLAND: Espebepe overhaul based on debt deal - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Espebepe overhaul based on debt deal - CEO.

text.p: Polish construction firm Espebepe SA has agreed on a plan to seek a debt write-off with its creditors, cut costs and improve operating margins in a bid to rescue the debt-ridden firm, its president said on Friday.
Andrzej Hass said the supervisory board of Espebepe, which reported a 51.5 million zloty loss in 1996 and is burdened with about 80 million in debts, accepted its restructuring plan on Wednesday.
"The key elements of the restructuring plan are to obtain the debt write-off deal...cut overhead costs and gain higher-margin orders," he told Reuters.
Hass said the firm wanted its biggest creditors, to write off 95 percent of the debts and smaller about 20 percent.
He said Espebepe would hold the first meeting with its creditors on March 14.
He said that the company would have to go bankrupt if creditors refused to accept the debt-write off deal.
"The basic condition is a success of the debt restructuring procedure...if it fails we'll be gone, but I believe the creditors will agree, I have signals that they will agree," Hass said.
He said the firm's biggest creditor was the state-owned Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA.
Hass said he hoped in 1997 the costs of the management would be reduced to 10 or 11 percent, down from 15 percent of total cost in 1996.
He said the company would seek to increase operating margins to 7.5 percent from last year's average of two percent and said the firm was already negotiating such deals with several foreign firms.
